about: Questions to the player, numbered once and never reused. The lead is the only writer. Wording is in play terms: what the original does, what ours does, what to do. answered rows keep their answer and outcome.

questions.title: Archers marking themselves as firing
questions.outcome: Merged 85611ebf: archers mark themselves firing as the original does.

questions.title: Soldiers changing places: whole rule vs the auto-resolved yardstick
questions.answer: auto-resolve weighs troop types; a fought battle has counters (crossbows one-shot knights, waste on peasants), so its verdict is no yardstick for a fought one
questions.outcome: Merged: the whole changing-places rule, oracle-checked; the fought check no longer demands the auto-resolve's winner.

questions.title: Do the computer's archers shoot while marching?
questions.answer: nothing to answer; waits on Q4
questions.outcome: Merged. On the field and lane your save was dealt, ours ends the no-orders battle exactly as the original did: 60 of 129 defenders left, attacker destroyed.

questions.title: One battle with no orders, saved at start and end
questions.outcome: Filed as noorders-start and noorders-end fixtures.

questions.title: Two End Turns in a game with Advanced Farming on
questions.inplay: Advanced Farming is the new-game option that changes how your fields work each season. Every save we have was played with it off, so those farming rules have never been checked against the original.
questions.todo: Start any new game with Advanced Farming on and play through two End Turns. Nothing else is needed. The game's own autosaves from that point are the two saves one turn apart the End Turn check needs; I will copy them from the install.
questions.ask: Reply: Q5 after the second End Turn
questions.outcome: Merged: your saves are the fifth End Turn pair. Every Advanced Farming rule the turn runs agrees; the one difference is the weather roll, which no save carries.

questions.title: Saving a game never finishes
questions.answer: type a name, click Save: the wait text appears, the dialog stays until thumbs-down, and Load lists no such game
questions.outcome: Merged: a refused save now repaints, as the original does. Saving mid-battle is its own row; Q9 asks which screen you were on.

questions.title: Relaunch the stopped siege-army work
questions.outcome: Merged: the siege residual was a defaulted save import, not an AI or battle rule; the End Turn check went from 271 to 278 of 279 fields.

questions.title: Relaunch the stopped screen-position audit
questions.outcome: Merged: every draw we could pair by coordinate sits exactly where the original draws it (115 of 115); the check is stored and tested. The near misses were the instrument's, not the screens'.

questions.title: When the save failed, was a battle on screen?
questions.inplay: In the original you can save from the battlefield menu bar in the middle of a battle. Ours refused that save silently, which looked like a hang. Both halves are now fixed and merged: a refused save repaints, and a mid-battle save writes and loads back onto the battlefield with the same battle running.
questions.todo: Only to confirm the diagnosis: were you on the battlefield or the campaign map when you typed the name and clicked Save? If the map, the cause is still unknown and I will reopen it.
questions.ask: Reply: Q9 battle, or Q9 map
questions.outcome: So the mid-battle refusal was not your case. The cause is still unknown; Q10 asks for one more try on a current build, which now shows what it refuses.

questions.title: Save once more from the campaign map on a current build
questions.inplay: Your save from the map wrote no file, and nothing we tried reproduced it. Two things changed since: a refused save now paints its reason instead of sitting on the wait text, and saving is no longer refused on the battlefield.
questions.todo: Build from current main, play to the campaign map, File then Save, type a name, click Save. Note exactly what the box shows next: the name in the Load list, or a message, and its words.
questions.ask: Reply: Q10 saved, or Q10 with the message shown
questions.outcome: The refusal did not recur. The three-second wait is filed and in flight; the original saves near instantly.

questions.title: After loading a save, should armies and merchants stand still for the first turn?
questions.inplay: In the original, when you start the program and load a save, merchants take one step at most and the AI's new armies do not march until the end of that first turn; from the second turn on everything moves normally. It is a defect in the original (the route data is not rebuilt on load); its own recordings show it. Ours now does the same. Loading a second save in the same session does not show it.
questions.todo: Choose: keep it (closer to the original), or fix it so everything moves on the first turn after a load.
questions.ask: Reply: Q11 keep, or Q11 fix

questions.title: How should we compare battles once dice are rolled?
questions.inplay: The AI's first decision in a battle rolls a die. The original and ours use different dice (ours is modern, which the new netcode needs), so from that first roll the two battles drift apart and one may win where the other loses. Everything up to the first roll now matches.
questions.todo: Choose: (a) during comparisons only, run our battles on the original's dice so whole battles can be compared move for move; (b) steer the original's dice to ours instead; (c) compare many battles and check the outcomes come out in the same proportions. (a) finds the most bugs and does not change the game you play.
questions.ask: Reply: Q12 a, b or c

questions.title: Does the choppy pointer depend on its size?
questions.inplay: Both the original and ours use the Windows pointer. Ours is drawn at the window's scale, 128 pixels square on your 4K screen, where the original's is 32. Windows can fall back to drawing a pointer that large itself, which can look choppy.
questions.todo: Play full screen and note whether the pointer is choppy; then run in a smaller window (so the pointer is smaller) and compare.
questions.ask: Reply: Q13 same, or Q13 smoother when small

questions.title: Should a freshly killed archer keep shooting?
questions.inplay: In the original, when the computer orders its archers to fire back, it can pick an archer who has just died and whose body is still on the field. That archer gets up, walks and keeps shooting at half strength until he is hit again. It is a defect in the original, read from its code, not yet seen on screen. Ours treats a dead archer as dead.
questions.todo: Choose: keep the original's behaviour (closer to the original), or leave dead archers dead.
questions.ask: Reply: Q14 keep, or Q14 dead

reports.text: The player starts on the east side of Quantville; in the original always west.
reports.outcome: Merged: each new game now re-rolls as the original does; west three games in four.

reports.text: Saving a game never finishes and no file appears.
reports.outcome: Fixed and merged twice over: a refused save repaints, and saving mid-battle now works as in the original (C237). Q9 asks which screen you were on, to confirm the cause.

reports.text: Saving takes about three seconds; should be near instant.
reports.outcome: Merged: the original's wait is 150 loops of an unthrottled loop, about a millisecond; ours now waits one tick.

reports.text: Tutorials come back on every launch.
reports.outcome: Merged: the toggle is remembered across launches, as the original keeps it in its options file.

reports.text: The AI raises three armies and they just sit; in the original the knight takes a county in the first year.
reports.outcome: Found: a new game gave each lord a castle in the books but not on the map, so the AI's levies marched to the town and stood there for ever. Also: the original does not attack in its first year either; the Knight launches in 1271. Fix delivered; oracle check and merge next session. Your current game keeps the flaw; a fresh game is right.

reports.text: The Knight never replied to a message.
reports.outcome: Found: the Knight wrote his reply and we threw it away before it reached your letters. Fix delivered with the idle-armies one.

reports.text: "No mercenaries in the army" shown for an army with mercenaries.
Army report screen text placement is off.
reports.outcome: Found four defects against the original's panel painter: the troop rows were piled two into one, the men total was missing, the three buttons sat a row too high, and an inset, the merchant name and the transport shield were absent. Fixed; oracle check and merge next session.

reports.text: Exit-game screen text placement is off.
reports.outcome: The box and buttons were exact; the prompt was upper-cased by ours and ran past the box. Fixed, same branch.

reports.text: Esc does not say "Exit the game, my lord?"
reports.outcome: The original speaks one of sixteen recorded lines when a confirm opens; ours now does on Esc. Same branch.

reports.text: The welcome line plays immediately at launch.
reports.outcome: Merged: it waits for the main menu to be the screen on top, as the original does. The trace diff missed it at first and caught it once it keyed sounds by the film before them.

reports.text: No red X when ordering troops to move in battle.
reports.outcome: Found blind by the trace diff and merged: the move marker, 30 ticks.

reports.text: The AI lord's shield does not disappear when it is done.
reports.outcome: Found blind by the pixel diff and merged: the shield rule, and the AI taking extra steps after the original would have finished (armies now ordered first and walking later, as the original).

reports.text: Zoomed-out map has water artifacts beyond the play square.
reports.outcome: Found blind by the pixel diff and merged: the coast and margin passes the original draws.

reports.text: A sad trumpet when winning a county.
reports.outcome: Found blind by the trace diff and merged: we had it backwards. The original plays the losing fanfare to the side that lost and nothing on a win; the victory fanfare file ships but is never played.

reports.text: Army wages and expected tax numbers are misaligned from their text.
reports.outcome: Found blind by the pixel diff on the Court screen: the two numbers sat about 100 px right of their labels. Fixed; every Court row now matches the original pixel for pixel. Merged.

reports.text: The mouse pointer moves at a reduced frame rate.
reports.outcome: Not measurable overnight (the machine was locked). Both games use the Windows pointer, so frame rate is not the cause. Lead: our pointer is 128x128 on your 4K screen, large enough that Windows may draw it in software. Q13 asks you to try it.
